note: Unselected T2D; four Phase 2 programs (GSK1292263, MBX-2982, PSN821, firuglipel/DS-8500a) rested on rodent OGTT and incretin-release models that over-predicted glucose lowering, and none passed Phase 2.
label: Type 2 diabetes (GPR119)

engagement.note: AR231453 raised glucose-dependent insulin release and oral glucose tolerance in wild-type but not GPR119-null mice; Chu 2008 added GLP-1/GIP release. No patient comparison.
engagement.quote: AR231453 also enhanced glucose-dependent insulin release in vivo and improved oral glucose tolerance in wild-type mice but not in GPR119-deficient mice.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level read; Chu 2008 (doi:10.1210/en.2007-0966, epub 2008-01-17) is the GLP-1/GIP readout paper.
engagement.judgement: The track opens on the Arena tool agonist AR231453 (not a member); it is the published model every member program cited, and the sponsors' own rodent data for GSK1292263 and PSN821 are unpublished or in a food-intake paper (Overton 2006, doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2006.02.004).

engagement.note: GSK1292263 for 14 days in T2D: total PYY rose ~25% (5-fold meal peaks) but total/active GLP-1, GIP, insulin and C-peptide were flat; the model's readouts did not move. Design: arms dosed alone and with metformin; GLP-1/GIP flat on GSK1292263 alone.
engagement.short: GLP-1/GIP/insulin flat in T2D; PYY rose
engagement.quote: GSK263 had no effect on active or total GLP-1 or GIP, but co-dosing with metformin increased post-prandial total GLP-1, with little effect on active GLP-1.
engagement.confidence_note: Open access, full text read. The sponsor's own rat GLP-1 data for GSK1292263 and the healthy-subject GLP-1/GIP augmentation are 'GlaxoSmithKline, unpublished data' (data not shown), so the published model side is the sibling agonist AR231453.
engagement.reason: GLP-1/GIP readout did not move in T2D
engagement.judgement: Scored contra because the readouts the mouse model used (plasma GLP-1, GIP, glucose-dependent insulin) did not move in 96 T2D patients dosed to steady state (100-600 mg/day), although the L-cell was engaged (total PYY WM-AUC +~25%). The alternative is same + partial on an 'L-cell secretion' readout; partial is recorded in source_calls_it. readout_tier is proximal because GLP-1 is the targeted cell's own secretory product (as acid is for a proton pump); downstream is the stricter reading. Not admissible here: MBX-2982 raised meal GLP-1 17% in T1D (Bilal 2025, doi:10.2337/db25-0096; wrong population) and in a 4-week T2D study known only from a press-release-derived database entry; PSN821 has no public PD data. The Nunez paper's own 'GSK263 was known to increase GLP-1 in animal models and healthy subjects' is a citation of unpublished data, not a stated side-by-side comparison, so comparison_stated is false and the model side is Chu 2008.
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma total and active GLP-1 and GIP weighted-mean AUC after standardized meals, vs placebo

engagement.model: Human primary colonic L-cell cultures (GLP-1/PYY secretion ex vivo)
engagement.note: Primary cultures from human colonic biopsies: GPR40/120 and GPBAR1 agonists raised GLP-1 1.5-fold, the GPR119 agonist AR231453 (10 nmol/l) did not. No member comparison yet.
engagement.short: Human L-cells: GPR119 agonist no GLP-1
engagement.quote: Agonists of G-protein-coupled receptor (GPR)40/120 and G-protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1 (GPBAR1) each increased GLP-1 release to 1.5-fold, but a GPR119 agonist did not significantly stimulate secretion.
engagement.confidence_note: Open access (PMC3648684), full text read. Received 2012-12-21, epub 2013-03-22, print June 2013. Only GLP-1 was assayed for the GPCR agonists; PYY was not tested with AR231453.
engagement.judgement: Opens the human ex-vivo track on the sibling tool agonist AR231453 (no member was run in human L-cells). Habib's own clinical remark ('some recent disappointing metabolic responses to GPR119 agonists in clinical trials') cites JNJ-38431055 (Katz 2012), a non-member, so no admissible comparison yet (decision 12).

engagement.model: Human primary colonic L-cell cultures (GLP-1/PYY secretion ex vivo)
engagement.note: GSK1292263 100-600 mg/day for 14 days in 96 T2D patients left total and active GLP-1 unchanged, as human L-cell cultures had shown for AR231453. Ruling: the human L-cell result (2013) was public after a GPR119-agonist engagement result in T2D patients (Katz 2012, JNJ-38431055), so it is a retrodiction; it reproduced GSK1292263's flat GLP-1, scored retro.
engagement.short: No GLP-1 ex vivo, none in T2D
engagement.quote: GSK263 had no effect on active or total GLP-1 or GIP, but co-dosing with metformin increased post-prandial total GLP-1, with little effect on active GLP-1.
engagement.confidence_note: Patient side open access, full text (quote checker-verified on the draft); model side full text read. The model compound is the sibling AR231453 at one concentration and the authors note human cultures were generally less responsive than murine ones, so the null is weakly powered. PYY, which rose five-fold in patients, was not tested with AR231453 ex vivo.
engagement.reason: Retrodiction: reproduced flat GLP-1 in T2D
engagement.judgement: Same: the one readout the human ex-vivo model gave for a GPR119 agonist (GLP-1 release) agreed with the member's patient PD. Paired, not stated: Habib 2013 cites 'disappointing metabolic responses ... in clinical trials' for JNJ-38431055 (Katz 2012), a non-member set aside under decision 12; no source sets Habib beside Nunez. Not a retrodiction: the model (received 2012-12-21, epub 2013-03-22) predates the member result (Nunez epub 2014-04-03), and the only human signal public then (Katz 2012, epub 2012-03-14) reported raised post-meal total GLP-1/GIP, the opposite of what Habib found. Not neg: the model's own data are for a non-member tool compound, so no member fell below a class bar in it. Efficacy is not scored on this track: the cultures read hormone release, not glucose. Settled under the 2026-11-09 retrodiction ruling: for engagement any drug's earlier patient result for the same target counts, and Katz 2012 (epub 2012-03-14) preceded Habib 2013, so retrodiction: true and status retro (it matched the member's flat GLP-1; its disagreement with Katz's non-member result is not scored).
engagement.magnitude_basis: GLP-1 release vs control ex vivo (AR231453 10 nmol/l, not significant) against plasma total and active GLP-1 weighted-mean AUC vs placebo in T2D (no effect)

dose.note: Oral AR231453 improved glucose tolerance in wild-type and diabetic KK-Ay mice; the regimen target is an orally active, glucose-dependent exposure. No human exposure yet. No model stated an exposure, occupancy or regimen target for a member drug, so dose stays untested.
dose.short: Oral mouse OGTT efficacy sets the target
dose.quote: Diabetic KK/A(y) mice were also highly responsive to AR231453.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level read; the mg/kg effective doses are in the full text and were not extracted.

efficacy.note: AR231453 improved oral glucose tolerance in wild-type and diabetic KK-Ay mice, GPR119-dependently; Overton 2006 had shown PSN632408 cut food intake and weight gain in rats.
efficacy.quote: Diabetic KK/A(y) mice were also highly responsive to AR231453.

efficacy.note: GSK1292263 100-600 mg/day for 14 days (96 T2D patients, alone or on metformin) lowered neither fasting nor 24-h glucose; the mouse OGTT prediction failed. Design: GSK1292263 given alone and, in some arms, with metformin; scored on the GSK1292263-alone comparison against placebo.
efficacy.short: No glucose lowering after 14 days in T2D
efficacy.quote: We conclude that GSK263 did not improve glucose control in type 2 diabetics, but it had profound effects on circulating PYY.
efficacy.confidence_note: Open access, full text read. Registry primaries for both studies were adverse events; 24-h weighted-mean glucose was the pharmacology gate, hence poc_gate. Registry results (NCT01119846 2018-01-17, NCT01128621 2017-10-16) post-date the paper.
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the class: the published mouse model (sibling agonist AR231453) and GSK's unpublished rat data predicted glucose lowering; 14-day dosing at steady-state exposures above the single-dose-active level gave none. MBX-2982 (NCT01035879, 4 weeks, 2009-10) and PSN821 (NCT01386099, 12 weeks, 2011) have no posted results and no peer-reviewed report; Nunez cites conference abstracts for glucose lowering with both, listed in patient_trials without a status.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: 24-h weighted-mean plasma glucose AUC vs placebo after 13-14 days

patient_trials.quote: After 13 days or 14 days of dosing, the BID and QD doses of GSK263 did not reduce plasma fasting glucose (data not shown) or glucose WM-AUC (0-24 h) in subjects with T2D, when compared with placebo.
GSK263 had no significant effect on circulating glucose, insulin, C-peptide or glucagon levels.

The GPR119 agonists MBX-2982 and PSN821 reduce fasting and post-prandial glucose levels in healthy subjects with fasting hyperglycemia or impaired glucose tolerance [44], [45] and in subjects with T2D [46], but these drugs may have off-target effects on gastric emptying.

efficacy.note: Firuglipel 12 weeks on metformin (US/Canada, n=298): HbA1c -0.08% vs placebo at 75 mg (p=0.57) while sitagliptin cut 0.43%; the Japanese monotherapy trial gave -0.44%, below sitagliptin. Design: firuglipel added to stable metformin against placebo, with sitagliptin as active control; scored on the HbA1c primary. Firuglipel's own track: the Japanese monotherapy trials met their primaries, the North-American add-on failed, so the track is contra.
efficacy.quote: Change From Baseline in Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) at Week 12: DS-8500a 75 mg vs Placebo LS Mean Difference -0.08 (95% CI -0.312 to 0.151), p=.566; Sitagliptin 100 mg vs Placebo -0.43 (-0.655 to -0.197), p=.002.
efficacy.confidence_note: The quote is assembled from the registry outcome-measure table (measure title, LS mean differences, CIs, p-values), not prose. Model side (Matsumoto 2018, rat OGTT and nSTZ repeat dosing) read at abstract level only: the JPET page returned 403 and the Firecrawl scrape 1.3 kB.
efficacy.reason: Firuglipel failed HbA1c add-on to metformin
efficacy.judgement: Firuglipel's own track on the mouse model (track = model x drug x route, so GSK1292263's contra no longer carries here). Model side is Chu 2007, public before any firuglipel trial; Matsumoto 2018 (DS-8500a in rats) was published after these trials and is scored on the nSTZ rat track as a retrodiction. The Japanese trials (Inagaki 2017 NCT02222350, 24-h WMG -1.05 mmol/L at 75 mg; Yamada 2018 NCT02628392, HbA1c -0.44%) met their primaries but are dated before this failure; the North-American metformin add-on trial failed its HbA1c primary while sitagliptin worked, and that latest result sets the track's status. Daiichi Sankyo dropped DS-8500a from its pipeline in May 2017 (portfolio decision, tier 5).

patient_trials.quote: DS-8500a demonstrated dose-dependent HbA1c lowering compared with placebo at week 12: change from baseline - 0.23% (p = 0.0173), - 0.37% (p = 0.0001), and - 0.44% (p < 0.0001) in the 25-mg, 50-mg, and 75-mg groups, respectively.
A significant dose-dependent reduction was observed in 24-h weighted mean glucose (linear: P = 0.0006, saturated at 25 mg: P = 0.0003, responded from 75 mg: P = 0.0176) when compared with the placebo

The 24-hour WMG decreased significantly after 28 days of treatment in the 10 mg and 75 mg groups with placebo-subtracted least squares mean differences (95% CI) of -0.74 (-1.29 to -0.19) mmol/L and -1.05 (-1.59 to -0.50) mmol/L, respectively.

efficacy.model: Neonatal-STZ diabetic rat, 2-week repeat dosing with OGTT (clinically tested members run as comparators)
efficacy.note: DS-8500a dosed beside GSK1292263 and MBX-2982 (30 mg/kg each, 14 days) in nSTZ rats, OGTT on days 0 and 14, to test loss of efficacy. Opens GSK1292263's rat track; firuglipel's rat track opens as an appended entry.
efficacy.short: nSTZ rat repeat-dose OGTT with comparators
efficacy.quote: In a repeat-dosing study, DS-8500a had statistically significant glucose-lowering effects at OGTT performed at the 1st day and after 2 weeks of treatment in neonatal streptozotocin-treated (nSTZ) rats
efficacy.confidence_note: Epub 2018-09-14 (print December 2018). Opening year is the publication date; the rat work itself predates the firuglipel trials but has no earlier public date.
efficacy.judgement: Own track, separate from the draft's mouse OGTT/incretin system (Chu 2007, model_id t2d-rodent-gpr119-ogtt): different species, an induced diabetic model, repeat dosing, and the clinically tested members run in it. The checker's rule question on splitting rat from mouse is left to the checker; this track scores only what the draft leaves unscored.

efficacy.model: Neonatal-STZ diabetic rat, 2-week repeat dosing with OGTT (clinically tested members run as comparators)
efficacy.note: Run after Nunez 2014: GSK1292263 and MBX-2982 (30 mg/kg) gave no significant OGTT glucose-AUC reduction on day 0 or 14 in nSTZ rats; DS-8500a did. Track: GSK1292263. Firuglipel, run in the same study, is scored as its own appended entry; MBX-2982 has no reported patient result.
efficacy.short: Failed member inactive in rat; reproduced
efficacy.quote: no statistically significant effects on the AUC PG were observed in the GSK1292263- or MBX2982-treated groups compared vehicle group.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read from a 2022-06-16 Wayback Machine capture of the JPET HTML (jpet.aspetjournals.org returns 403; the ScienceDirect copy paywalls the Results); quote spelling ('MBX2982', 'compared vehicle') as in the source. All three compounds at 30 mg/kg; MBX-2982 exposure exceeded DS-8500a's (Supplemental Table 3), GSK1292263's rat exposure is not given in the text read.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): Daiichi chose the comparators because they 'had already been studied in clinical stages' and cites the GSK1292263 phase 2 failure (Nunez 2014) in the introduction, so the run post-dates the known answer; the paper states the comparison ('These observations seem to differ from the clinical results showing that a single dose of GSK1292263 (25-800 mg) had a tendency to reduce glucose incremental AUC during OGTT, although there was no reduction in weighted-mean glucose AUC after 13 or 14 days of dosing'). The model reproduced the 14-day result (no significant glucose lowering by GSK1292263 on day 0 or day 14), so retro, not same; the checker's missing-list reading that the comparators 'still lowered glucose' rests on the abstract and is not what the Results say. Partial per the source: the single-dose arm differs (single human doses tended to cut OGTT glucose; the rat single dose was numerically lower, not significant). MBX-2982's own clinical result (NCT01035879, no posted results) is unreported, so the retro rests on GSK1292263 alone. The model's prospective call for DS-8500a (met HbA1c and 24-h WMG primaries in Japan, failed the North-American metformin add-on trial) is already scored on the draft's rodent track (efficacy index 3, safety index 2, model_src this paper) and is not duplicated here; if the checker splits rat from mouse, those entries belong on this track.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: OGTT glucose AUC(0-3 h) vs vehicle after 14 days in nSTZ rats, against 24-h weighted-mean glucose AUC vs placebo after 13-14 days in T2D (Nunez 2014), both null for GSK1292263

patient_trials.quote: After 13 days or 14 days of dosing, the BID and QD doses of GSK263 did not reduce plasma fasting glucose (data not shown) or glucose WM-AUC (0-24 h) in subjects with T2D, when compared with placebo.

efficacy.note: Opens firuglipel's track on the mouse model; proxy year, the pairing was open from firuglipel's first trial (NCT02222350, 2014). No comparison until its trials.
efficacy.short: Firuglipel track opens on mouse model
efficacy.quote: Diabetic KK/A(y) mice were also highly responsive to AR231453.
efficacy.judgement: Opener appended for the firuglipel track; year set to the track's first comparison year so the track stays in year order without reordering existing entries.

efficacy.model: Neonatal-STZ diabetic rat, 2-week repeat dosing with OGTT (clinically tested members run as comparators)
efficacy.note: Opens firuglipel's nSTZ rat track: DS-8500a dosed beside GSK1292263 and MBX-2982 (30 mg/kg, 14 days), OGTT on days 0 and 14.
efficacy.quote: In a repeat-dosing study, DS-8500a had statistically significant glucose-lowering effects at OGTT performed at the 1st day and after 2 weeks of treatment in neonatal streptozotocin-treated (nSTZ) rats
efficacy.confidence_note: Epub 2018-09-14 (print December 2018). Opening year is the publication date; the rat work itself predates the firuglipel trials but has no earlier public date.
efficacy.judgement: Own track, separate from the draft's mouse OGTT/incretin system (Chu 2007, model_id t2d-rodent-gpr119-ogtt): different species, an induced diabetic model, repeat dosing, and the clinically tested members run in it. The checker's rule question on splitting rat from mouse is left to the checker; this track scores only what the draft leaves unscored.

efficacy.model: Neonatal-STZ diabetic rat, 2-week repeat dosing with OGTT (clinically tested members run as comparators)
efficacy.note: Matsumoto 2018 (Sept) showed sustained DS-8500a glucose lowering in nSTZ rats after firuglipel's patient results were public; it matched the Japanese monotherapy trials but not the North-American metformin add-on failure (May 2018), so the retrodiction failed: contra.
efficacy.short: Rat lowering vs firuglipel add-on failure
efficacy.quote: Change From Baseline in Glycated Hemoglobin (HbA1c) at Week 12: DS-8500a 75 mg vs Placebo LS Mean Difference -0.08 (95% CI -0.312 to 0.151), p=.566; Sitagliptin 100 mg vs Placebo -0.43 (-0.655 to -0.197), p=.002.
efficacy.confidence_note: Model side abstract (Europe PMC, PMID 30217957): 'In a repeat-dosing study, DS-8500a had statistically significant glucose-lowering effects at OGTT performed at the 1st day and after 2 weeks of treatment in neonatal streptozotocin-treated (nSTZ) rats'. Patient quote assembled from the registry outcome table.
efficacy.reason: Rat efficacy not reproduced in add-on trial
efficacy.judgement: Split from efficacy 5 (one study, several member drugs whose patients differ). Retrodiction by post-dating (efficacy counts any earlier patient result for the target, here also firuglipel's own). Scored contra rather than retro because the latest public firuglipel result, the North-American add-on failure, was not reproduced; the Japanese monotherapy successes were (source_calls_it partial).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: OGTT glucose AUC vs vehicle after 14 days in nSTZ rats (significant, greater than GSK1292263 and MBX-2982) against placebo-adjusted HbA1c at week 12 on metformin (-0.08%, p=0.57)

safety.note: Stated prediction: insulin release is glucose-dependent, so hypoglycaemia should be rare. Routine rodent and dog toxicology for GSK1292263 was later reported silent on muscle (Nunez 2014). Opens firuglipel's safety track on this model (the class prediction, paired with firuglipel's trials).
safety.quote: Additionally, we show here that GPR119 functions as a glucose-dependent insulinotropic receptor.

safety.note: Firuglipel 10 or 75 mg for 28 days in 99 Japanese T2D patients: well tolerated, no hypoglycaemia; Yamada 2018 (12 weeks, n=368) later reported two drug-related hypoglycaemia cases at 50 mg. Dated to the earliest public comparison (Inagaki 2017); the glucose-dependence prediction held.
safety.quote: Both doses of DS-8500a were well tolerated without significant treatment-related adverse events, hypoglycemia, or discontinuations due to adverse events.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level read of Inagaki 2017 (epub 2017-09-29; NCT02222350, no posted registry results) and Yamada 2018 (epub 2018-02-27). Model side is Chu 2007; Matsumoto 2018 (DS-8500a in fasted rats) post-dates both trials.
safety.reason: Glucose-dependent action held; no missed harm
safety.judgement: Same on the one stated safety prediction (glucose-dependent insulinotropism, hence low hypoglycaemia risk), which Chu 2007 made for the class and Matsumoto 2018 later for firuglipel itself (after the trials, so not the model side here). Silence not contradicted: GSK1292263 produced one myalgia case at 600 mg QD with normal CK where rodent and dog toxicology had shown no muscle toxicity (Nunez 2014); a single case is not scored. He 2013 (doi:10.5414/CP201949) reports hERG-predicted QT prolongation in a first-in-man T2D drug but does not name it, so it cannot be tied to a member.

safety.model: In-vitro human transporter and CYP inhibition panel (BCRP, OATP1B1/1B3, Pgp, OCT2, CYP1A2/2C9/2C19/2D6/3A4) for statin drug interaction
safety.note: In vitro, GSK1292263 inhibited BCRP and OATP1B1 (IC50 >30 µM for CYPs, Pgp, OATP1B3, OCT2), flagging a possible statin interaction before the clinical DDI study.
safety.short: In-vitro panel flags BCRP/OATP1B1 statin DDI
safety.quote: However, GSK1292263 inhibited BCRP and OATP1B1, which are transporters involved in statin disposition.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level read (Xenobiotica, paywalled). Epub 2012-12-21, print June 2013; the in-vitro work preceded the clinical study (NCT01101568, April-June 2010) but has no earlier public date, so 2012 is a proxy.
safety.judgement: Scope call for the checker: an in-vitro human transporter/CYP panel is the regulator-standard model for a drug-drug-interaction harm, so it is entered as a safety track; it predicts a molecule-specific off-target liability of one member, not the mechanism, hence prediction_level 'class' only for want of a better value. model_kind ex_vivo is the nearest enum for human recombinant-transporter and microsomal assays.

safety.model: In-vitro human transporter and CYP inhibition panel (BCRP, OATP1B1/1B3, Pgp, OCT2, CYP1A2/2C9/2C19/2D6/3A4) for statin drug interaction
safety.note: Healthy-subject DDI study: GSK1292263 300 mg BID raised simvastatin AUC 1.34x and rosuvastatin 1.39x (intestinal BCRP/CYP3A4), but simvastatin acid 1.05x showed no OATP1B1 inhibition.
safety.short: BCRP DDI held; OATP1B1 did not
safety.quote: were observed when co-administered with GSK1292263, which is consistent with an inhibitory effect on intestinal BCRP and CYP3A4. In contrast, GSK1292263 did not inhibit OATP1B1 based on the lack of changes in simvastatin acid exposure
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level read; the source itself states the in-vitro-to-clinical comparison. Clinical arm NCT01101568 (healthy subjects, completed 2010-06-24) has no registry results. The abstract gives IC50 bands, not a predicted AUC ratio, so magnitude is direction only.
safety.reason: Weak statin DDI as flagged; half mechanism
safety.judgement: Same with partial (decision 11): the stated prediction, a statin interaction through BCRP and OATP1B1, held in direction (1.34-1.39x AUC, weak) by the BCRP/CYP3A4 route, while the OATP1B1 component did not translate (simvastatin acid 1.05x). The alternative reading is contra, magnitude opposite, on the OATP1B1 call alone; rejected because the harm the panel flagged (raised statin exposure) did appear and the source calls the interaction weak and mechanistically explained. Healthy volunteers, not T2D patients: no MONDO import, since healthy subjects are not another indication.
safety.magnitude_basis: statin AUC(0-inf) ratio with GSK1292263 300 mg BID (simvastatin 1.34, rosuvastatin 1.39, simvastatin acid 1.05) against in-vitro BCRP and OATP1B1 inhibition; no predicted ratio in the abstract
